title: Adaptive symptom fingerprinting and multi-signal alert composer for SLO precision
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Problem: Our current SLO alerting frequently produces noisy pages for transient downstream errors and misses correlated degradations across traces/metrics/logs. We need an orchestration layer that composes signals and reasons about a feature-level symptom instead of firing on single-rule thresholds.

Goal: Build an ‘alert composer’ that ingests enriched traces, metric aggregates, and log-error signatures to produce a compact symptom fingerprint. Use that fingerprint to: (1) compute burn-rate signals with context-aware gating, (2) score anomalies with a multi-signal model, and (3) apply configurable paging policies (throttle, silence, escalate). The system must integrate light-weight tracing hooks to capture span-level error annotations without increasing tail latency, and must work within existing telemetry pipelines (Kafka -> processor -> bigquery/metrics store/Grafana).

Constraints: Minimal added latency (<1ms p50) on hot RPC paths for hook instrumentation; storage/backpressure limits in the telemetry pipeline; backwards-compatible with existing SLO rules so ops can opt-in per-service. Design must support per-tenant SLO partitioning and explicit fallbacks when enriched signals are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Composer produces a canonical symptom fingerprint for >=95% of alert candidates in the staging cluster
Burn-rate alerts powered by composer reduce total PagerDuty pages by >=30% in a two-week pilot while maintaining SLO coverage
Tracing hooks add <1.0ms p50 latency on instrumented RPCs measured under 90th percentile load
Anomaly score output stored in metrics backend with retention and can be queried by Grafana panels
Configurable paging policy rules available in Console rollout for at least three services (payments, inference, console)
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design workshop - finalize symptom fingerprint schema, field names, and signal weighting. Produce Confluence design doc.
Week 2: Implement lightweight trace hook lib (Go/Python) that emits compact annotations to telemetry topic; add CI microbenchmarks.
Week 3: Processor: extend Kafka enrichment stage to join metric aggregates + log-error signatures and compute fingerprint; implement anomaly scorer prototype (rule-weight + simple ML ensemble).
Week 4: Persist fingerprint and anomaly_score to metrics store; expose queryable labels and build Grafana dashboard templates for feature owners.
Week 5: Integrate composer with existing burn-rate engine: add gating and decider that uses fingerprint confidence and anomaly_score to escalate or suppress alerts.
Week 6: Pilot with two non-critical services, collect telemetry, iterate on thresholds and paging policies; run controlled drill to validate pages and runbooks.
Post-pilot: Roll out Console UI controls for per-service policy toggles and release observability-2026.03
